name: Unsecured Parking Theft
summary: Cargo is taken from a stationary vehicle at an unsecured stop, most often during a statutory rest period at night. This is the highest-volume cargo crime pattern in European road freight and it is overwhelmingly a function of where and when a vehicle stops rather than of who is carrying it.
how_it_works: A loaded vehicle stops at a lay-by, service area or industrial estate that has no access control, lighting or surveillance.
The stop is typically driven by driving-time regulation rather than chosen for security, which makes it predictable.
Curtains are cut or doors are opened while the driver rests, frequently without the driver being aware.
Cargo is removed in minutes into a following vehicle.
The loss is often discovered only at delivery, by which time the location and time window are uncertain.

indicators.signal: Planned route and schedule force a rest period in a corridor segment with no certified secure parking within range
indicators.observable_in: Route plan compared against secure parking availability
indicators.notes: This is the key preventable exposure, and it is visible before the vehicle ever moves.

indicators.signal: High value-density commodity is planned to move in a soft-sided trailer
Overnight stop recorded at a location that is not a certified secure parking area
indicators.observable_in: Telematics stop location against secure parking registry

indicators.signal: Stop duration of several hours in a known high-incidence corridor segment
indicators.observable_in: Telematics dwell analysis against incident geography

indicators.signal: Trailer door or curtain sensor triggers during a rest period
Loss discovered at delivery with no identified stop, indicating that stop-level visibility is absent
indicators.notes: Not an indicator of the crime so much as of a control gap that makes this pattern viable and unattributable.

false_positives.looks_like: A long unplanned stop in a high-risk area.
false_positives.actually: A breakdown, traffic incident, border queue or enforced congestion stop, none of which the driver chose.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Correlate with breakdown and incident reports and with traffic data for the corridor before treating a stop as a policy breach.

false_positives.actually: Accidental damage from loading equipment or road debris, which is common on soft-sided equipment.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Compare the cut geometry and location with the load plan, and verify against seal and count records whether anything is actually missing.

preventive: Plan routes so that every statutory rest falls within reach of a certified secure parking area, and treat a route that cannot meet this as an exception requiring approval.
Move high value-density commodities in hard-sided or rigid equipment rather than soft-sided trailers.
Prohibit overnight stops in identified high-incidence corridor segments through contractual route and stop policy, not through guidance alone.
Where a soft-sided trailer is unavoidable, fit anti-slash curtain material and intrusion detection.
detective: Geofence certified secure parking areas and alert on any rest period taken outside them.
Alert on stop duration above a corridor-specific threshold in segments with elevated incident history.
Fit and monitor door and curtain sensors so that the loss is detected at the stop rather than at the delivery.
responsive: Report immediately with the precise stop location and time window, since recovery and investigation both depend on narrowing these.
Feed the confirmed location back into route and parking policy, so that corridor risk assessment reflects observed rather than assumed exposure.
Review whether the schedule itself made a compliant secure stop impossible, and correct the planning rule rather than the driver.

regulatory_hooks.relevance: A documented risk analysis of direct suppliers must identify this pattern class where the carrier population plausibly exposes the company to it.
Preventive measures listed here are the kind of control a company is expected to define and evidence once the risk is identified.
Mandatory rest periods determine where and when a loaded vehicle must stop, which is what makes this exposure structural and therefore plannable.
